canonical.title: Toolchain fit: which Linux distro costs least setup work for .NET 10 + TypeScript + Docker in 2026

parent.title: Which Linux to switch to in 2026: a decision framework for a .NET developer leaving Windows

siblings.title: The 2026 Linux distro landscape: what actually differs between the families
siblings.summary: There are only five real distro families, and for a Windows developer moving to Linux in 2026 the honest shortlist is Fedora Workstation, Ubuntu LTS, Linux Mint, Bluefin/Aurora, and openSUSE Tumbleweed — everything else is a variation, a server OS, or a hobby.

siblings.title: Stable, rolling, or atomic: picking a release model for your first Linux daily driver
siblings.summary: Start on a 6-month fixed release (Fedora Workstation) or an atomic Fedora image (Bluefin DX); avoid pure rolling and avoid Debian stable — and here is the evidence for each release model's breakage, rollback, and software-age tradeoffs.

siblings.title: Picking a Linux desktop in 2026: the Windows 11 switcher's decision guide
siblings.summary: KDE Plasma is the lowest-friction landing spot for a Windows 11 developer in 2026; X11 sessions die this year, so the real choice is which Wayland compositor's rough edges you can live with.

siblings.title: Hardware and driver reality in 2026: only three things should decide your distro
siblings.summary: In 2026 only three hardware classes still force a distro choice — NVIDIA, very new silicon, and Secure-Boot dual-boot; everything else is a live-USB check away.

siblings.title: Windows to Linux in 2026: what crosses over, what doesn't, and how to stage the switch
siblings.summary: Almost everything a .NET developer does crosses to Linux in 2026 — the four things that don't are desktop Office with VBA, a native Outlook with working calendar, WPF/WinForms designers, and Windows-only compliance tooling.

siblings.title: Linux upkeep in 2026: support windows, upgrade pain, and monthly chores ranked
siblings.summary: Ranked by ongoing upkeep for a learning-level Linux user: atomic Fedora and Ubuntu/Mint LTS are near-zero chore; Fedora Workstation costs one upgrade a year; Arch costs a reading habit you cannot skip.

siblings.title: Gaming and media on Linux in 2026: singleplayer is solved, anti-cheat and DRM streaming are not
siblings.summary: Roughly 90% of Windows Steam titles launch under Proton; the two real losses are kernel anti-cheat multiplayer and browser DRM streaming above 720p SDR.

sources.title: Install .NET on Linux — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Microsoft publishes .NET packages at packages.microsoft.com only for Azure Linux, Debian, openSUSE Leap and SLES; Alpine, CentOS Stream, Fedora, RHEL and Ubuntu publish their own.

sources.title: .NET on Ubuntu: which feed to use — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Canonical now owns .NET on Ubuntu; Ubuntu 26.04 has .NET 10 in the built-in feed and 9.0/8.0 only via the dotnet/backports PPA, and Canonical SDKs are always in the .1xx feature band.

sources.title: Install .NET on Fedora — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Fedora 43 and 44 support .NET 10, 9 and 8 via dnf, but Microsoft warns packages can lag the .NET release.

sources.title: Install .NET on Debian — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Debian 12 and 13 get .NET 10/9/8 by registering packages.microsoft.com via the packages-microsoft-prod.deb.

sources.title: Install .NET on openSUSE — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Only openSUSE Leap 16 is a supported .NET target, installed from the Microsoft zypper repo, and its packages depend on OpenSSL 3.x.

sources.title: Troubleshoot .NET Linux package mix-ups — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: Mixing distro and Microsoft .NET feeds produces libhostfxr.so / FrameworkList.xml failures; the fix is apt/dnf pinning.

sources.title: dotnet-sdk-10.0 — Fedora Packages
sources.claim: Fedora 43 and 44 ship dotnet-sdk-10.0 at version 10.0.110, i.e. the .1xx feature band.

sources.title: dotnet packages — Arch Linux
sources.claim: Arch's [extra] repo carries dotnet-sdk 10.0.10.sdk110 plus side-by-side dotnet-sdk-8.0/9.0/10.0 packages.

sources.title: dotnet/sdk issue 52253 — No match for argument: dotnet-sdk-10.0
sources.claim: Users hit 'No match for argument: dotnet-sdk-10.0' on RPM distros more than a month after the .NET 10 release.

sources.title: Scripted and manual .NET installs — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: dotnet-install.sh and tarball installs leave you to install dependencies, export DOTNET_ROOT/PATH and update manually; they are the only route to preview SDKs.

sources.title: Install the .NET SDK snap — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: The .NET SDK snap is provided and maintained by Canonical, giving a distro-agnostic install path.

sources.title: nodejs — Ubuntu Packages
sources.claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS ships nodejs 22.22.1; 24.04 ships 18.19.1 and 22.04 ships 12.22.9.

sources.title: nodejs22 — Fedora Packages
sources.claim: Fedora 44 ships nodejs22 at 22.22.2, one LTS line behind current Node LTS.

sources.title: nodesource/distributions
sources.claim: NodeSource maintains third-party apt and dnf repositories carrying current Node.js majors.

sources.title: mise — Getting Started
sources.claim: mise installs via a one-line curl script into ~/.local/bin and pulls tools from multiple backends.

sources.title: bun — Installation
sources.claim: bun installs from its own script on any distro, needs unzip and glibc 2.17+, and the default x64 build requires AVX2.

sources.title: pnpm — Installation
sources.claim: pnpm can be installed standalone without Node.js present, or via Corepack/npm when Node v22+ is present.

sources.title: Install Docker Engine — Docker Docs
sources.claim: Docker Engine has official install procedures only for CentOS, Debian, Fedora, RHEL, Ubuntu and Raspberry Pi OS.

sources.title: Install Docker Desktop on Linux — Docker Docs
sources.claim: Docker Desktop for Linux is officially supported on Ubuntu, Debian, RHEL and Fedora only, with an untested experimental Arch package, and requires KVM plus GNOME/KDE/MATE.

sources.title: docker packages — Arch Linux
sources.claim: Arch's [extra] repo tracks Docker closely: docker 29.6.2, docker-compose 5.3.1 and docker-buildx 0.35.0 as of July 2026.

sources.title: SELinux and containers — Ryan Martin
sources.claim: On SELinux-enforcing distros bind mounts fail with permission denied unless volumes carry :z/:Z or are relabelled to container_file_t.

sources.title: Installing Docker on Silverblue — Fedora Discussion
sources.claim: Layering docker-ce on Fedora Silverblue works but needs manual .repo placement, and community members point to preinstalled Podman instead.

sources.title: Bluefin DX — Bluefin Docs
sources.claim: Bluefin's developer image ships docker-ce with the Compose and Buildx plugins plus Podman tooling and VS Code with Dev Containers preconfigured.

sources.title: Rider installation guide — JetBrains
sources.claim: Rider 2026.1 supports Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 LTS, Fedora 43/44, Debian 13 and Amazon Linux 2023 with glibc 2.28+; JetBrains flags snap performance degradation.

sources.title: JetBrains Toolbox App installation
sources.claim: JetBrains Toolbox on Linux is a distro-agnostic tarball you unpack yourself.

sources.title: Visual Studio Code on Linux
sources.claim: VS Code ships official deb, rpm (also covering openSUSE/SLE) and snap packages; Arch AUR and nixpkgs builds are community-maintained, and Flatpak is not an official channel.

sources.title: VS Code Flatpak is useless — Lobsters
sources.claim: Developer consensus is that the sandboxed VS Code Flatpak is unfit for real development.

sources.title: The VS Code Flatpak problem — bentsukun.ch
sources.claim: The VS Code Flatpak cannot see host toolchains and cannot reach /var/run/docker.sock by default.

sources.title: Ghostty — binary installation
sources.claim: Ghostty is first-party packaged for Arch [extra], Alpine, Gentoo, Nix, Solus, Void and snap; Fedora and Ubuntu rely on COPR/community debs and openSUSE dropped it over Zig versioning.

sources.title: Install kubectl on Linux — Kubernetes
sources.claim: kubectl installs from pkgs.k8s.io apt/dnf/zypper repos pinned per minor version.

sources.title: Install Terraform — HashiCorp Developer
sources.claim: Terraform installs from HashiCorp's own apt and dnf repositories on Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL.

sources.title: Announcing the HashiCorp Linux repository
sources.claim: HashiCorp maintains a first-party Linux repository covering Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL/CentOS and Amazon Linux only.

sources.title: Coolify installation docs
sources.claim: Coolify's server-side installer supports Debian-based and RHEL-based hosts, so the workstation only needs docker CLI plus SSH.

sources.title: Coolify Terraform provider
sources.claim: A Coolify Terraform provider exists covering applications, databases, servers and env vars, requiring an API token enabled in the dashboard.

sources.title: Install PowerShell on Ubuntu — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: PowerShell 7 on Linux is installed from the Microsoft apt/dnf/zypper repositories, the preferred method.

sources.title: Homebrew on Linux
sources.claim: Homebrew on Linux needs a working system C compiler and recent glibc/gcc, is single-user, and uses sudo only during install.

sources.title: dotnet/core discussion 9556 — Linux distribution selection policy
sources.claim: Which Linux distributions get Microsoft .NET packages is governed by a published selection policy.

sources.title: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS release schedule — OMG! Ubuntu
sources.claim: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 'Resolute Raccoon' released on 23 April 2026.

sources.title: NixOS/nixpkgs
sources.claim: nixpkgs is the package set behind Nix, usable as an overlay package manager on any distro.
